propranolol, a beta-adrenoceptor antagonist, did not affect the swimming endurance performance of rats.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
propranolol does not enhance endurance performance in rats.
beta-adrenoreceptor blockade does not enhance physical endurance in rats.
propranolol is not an ergogenic aid.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
beta-receptor blockade by propranolol is a non-essential mechanism for the development of physical endurance.
propranolol, but not PBZ, has a significant effect on exercise-induced lactacidaemia and that propranolols overall effect on swimming endurance is not as beneficial as that of exercise alone.
propranolol does not improve physical endurance and skeletal muscle pulling strength, and that it antagonises lactacidaemia, but PBZ does not affect endurance performance, SMG and BLA levels.
The main takeaway from our work is that
beta-blockers do not improve endurance exercise performance in rats.
propranolol, but not phenoxybenamine, antagonised the exercise-induced lactacidaemia.
beta-receptor antagonists are not effective in improving physical performance.
